title: Mass in Kilograms and Grams
introduction: Build on Primary 1 knowledge and practise mass in kilograms and grams.
definition: Mass is measured in grams (g) and kilograms (kg). Use a balance or scale, read its markings and estimate by comparing with known masses. One kilogram equals 1,000 grams.

visuals.label: 1 kg = 1,000 g
visuals.description: Equal masses expressed in different units.
visuals.alt: 1 kg = 1,000 g — Equal masses expressed in different units.

examples.question: A scale shows 450 g for a bag.
A parcel feels about as heavy as two 1 kg reference masses.

exercises.question: A scale shows 750 g. Mass in g?
exercises.solution: The scale reading is 750 and its unit is grams, giving 750 g.

exercises.question: Which unit suits a school bag: g or kg?
exercises.solution: A school bag typically weighs several kilograms, so kg is a convenient unit.

exercises.question: Which is heavier, 300 g or 800 g? Enter grams.
A box is about twice as heavy as a 500 g reference. Estimate grams.
A scale shows 3 kg. Mass in kg?
exercises.solution: The scale reading is 3 and its unit is kilograms, giving 3 kg.

summary: Mass is measured in grams (g) and kilograms (kg). Use a balance or scale, read its markings and estimate by comparing with known masses. One kilogram equals 1,000 grams.
